statements.markdown:
**Proposition 2.1 (compact-strip regularity).** For $\gamma\in\mathcal U$
and $0\le T<1$, the value has bounded, jointly continuous spatial derivatives
of every positive finite order on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R$. If admissible
coefficients converge in $L^1$ and their smooth, even, convex, one-Lipschitz
terminal values converge uniformly to $|x|$, these spatial derivatives
converge uniformly on each such strip. The bounds depend on the derivative
order, the fixed strip and a common coefficient mass bound. Time derivatives need only exist
almost everywhere across coefficient jumps. On an open constant interval,
the heat formula supplies the additional time smoothness used in §4.
The terminal estimate is
$$
|x|\le\Phi_\gamma(t,x)
\le |x|+\sqrt{2(1-t)/\pi}+\frac12\int_t^1\gamma(s)\,ds.
$$

statements.markdown:
We first regard the value as a function of the starting state, holding
$t$ and $\gamma$ fixed, and write $\Phi=\Phi_\gamma$. Given a permitted
control, use the same responses to each Brownian history at two starting
states $x$ and $y$. The costs are unchanged, and the triangle inequality
bounds the change in the terminal reward by $|x-y|$, so taking the
supremum over controls gives

$$
|\Phi_\gamma(t,x)-\Phi_\gamma(t,y)|\le |x-y|.
$$

The value is also **convex**: between two states its graph lies at or
below the chord joining their values. Indeed,
each fixed-control payoff is an average of translated absolute-value
functions, hence convex. Its chord lies at or below the chord of the
best endpoint payoffs, and taking the supremum preserves that upper bound.

[OpenAI (2026a), Lemmas 2.1–2.2][support-regularity] supply spatial
differentiability below time one.

$-\gamma(s)(\alpha_s-\Phi_x(s,Y_s))^2/2$. It is nonpositive, and is zero
for the feedback control.
